title: The Echo of Halcyon Drift
premise: Oscar Marchetti, an insurance investigator who catalogues impossible accidents aboard the cargo hauler Halcyon Drift, discovers that the colony's children are all dreaming the same dream: a signal rising from dead space that shouldn't exist. The dreams turn out to be echoes of a lost generation ship's memory core—memories that include Oscar's own erased past as one of its crew. Racing a closing jump window, Oscar and the children's teacher, Amara Voss, must reach the edge-of-dead-space relay to answer the signal before corporate salvagers silence it forever. In the end, Oscar chooses to broadcast the ship's memories to every colony in contested space, sacrificing his anonymity and his clean record, but keeping the truth—and his love for Amara—alive.
about_author: Paloma Brightwater is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who spent six years writing incident reports before turning them into fiction. She lives on a houseboat with a malfunctioning weather satellite and writes stories about people who refuse to stay invisible.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Oscar Marchetti investigates a 'freak' decompression on the Halcyon Drift and notices something stranger than sabotage: the colony's children all describe the same dream—a green light singing from dead space. Through Oscar's wary, procedural POV, we learn he's spent five years erasing traces of his own history. Emotional beat: unease, as the impossible accident mirrors a memory he doesn't know he has.

chapters.title: What the Relay Remembers
chapters.summary: Amara Voss, the schoolteacher whose students can't sleep, brings Oscar a child's drawing of the relay station—drawn from inside it. When Oscar touches the sketch, fragments of a generation ship's memory core surface: his own face, younger, wearing a crew insignia. POV alternates between Oscar and Amara. Emotional beat: vertigo and reluctant intimacy, as two guarded people realize the dream is a message meant for him.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Live Signal
chapters.summary: Corporate salvagers arrive to seize the children and scrub the signal; Oscar and Amara steal the Halcyon Drift and burn for the relay, racing the jump window. Aboard, the memory core floods back—Oscar helped erase the ship's records to protect its survivors, including himself. POV shifts to Amara watching Oscar choose between duty to his employers and the truth. Emotional beat: desperate momentum and confession under fire.

chapters.title: The Echo Answers
chapters.summary: At the relay, with salvagers closing and the window seconds from closing, Oscar must decide: restore his erased identity privately or broadcast the generation ship's memories to every colony. He broadcasts everything—the children's dream fulfilled, the cover-up exposed—at the cost of his record and his invisibility. In the quiet after, Amara takes his hand. Emotional beat: catharsis; identity reclaimed not as a secret kept but as a truth shared.
